explain.say: Warm blood loses heat wherever skin meets air. Large, thin body parts like ears have lots of skin for their size, so they lose heat quickly.

explain.say: This pattern is called Allen's rule: animals in cold places tend to have shorter ears, tails and limbs than their relatives in hot places. African elephants' huge ears work like the fennec's.

faq.q: Why does a fennec fox have big ears?
faq.a: Its ears, up to about 15 centimetres long, are full of blood vessels that give off heat, cooling the fox in the desert. They also help it hear insects and small animals moving under the sand.
asks: How do big ears keep a fox cool?

faq.q: Why does an Arctic fox have small ears?
faq.a: Small, furry ears have little surface for heat to escape. Together with a short muzzle, short legs and very thick fur, they help the Arctic fox keep warm in temperatures far below freezing.
asks: How does an Arctic fox stay warm?
Why does the Arctic fox change colour?

faq.a: Allen's rule, named after the zoologist Joel Asaph Allen in 1877, says that warm-blooded animals in cold climates tend to have shorter limbs, ears and tails than related animals in warm climates, to save or lose heat.
asks: Why do cold animals have short legs?

faq.a: Bergmann's rule says that within related animals, those in colder places tend to be larger. A bigger body has less surface for its volume, so it keeps heat better. It is a trend, with many exceptions.
asks: Why are animals bigger in cold places?
What is surface area to volume ratio?

faq.q: Why do elephants flap their ears?
faq.a: African elephants have huge ears full of blood vessels. Flapping them moves air over the thin skin, cooling the blood, which then flows back into the body. It works like the fennec fox's ears.
asks: Why do African elephants have bigger ears than Asian elephants?

facts: The fennec fox has the largest ears relative to body size of any fox.
Allen's rule was proposed by the American zoologist Joel Asaph Allen in 1877.
